claims.text: The local release and selected-lines snapshot record the Trade Please campaign window as February 10 through July 31, 1998.

Bulbapedia's Trade Please! page says participants mailed a flyer included with the Suzukisan Trade Please CD, any two Pokemon trading cards, and a return envelope to MediaFactory, then selected one course.

The selected-lines snapshot records A Course as Charizard plus Trade Please!, B Course as Blastoise plus Trade Please!, and C Course as Venusaur plus Trade Please!. The release models four source-pinned card identities, not a claim that one participant received all four in one mailing.

The local rows credit Venusaur, Charizard, and Blastoise to Ken Sugimori and Trade Please! to Imakuni? as source/provider metadata; those credits orient catalog memory but do not authenticate a physical card.

Trade Please matters because the market behavior becomes the object: the participant literally traded cards through the mail, and the campaign returned a card about trading plus one chosen Kanto starter prize.

Agents must preserve the mail-in campaign route, course pairing, source row 033-036 identities, CD/flyer route, starter prize row, Trade Please! special-back identity, and the difference from CD Promo, Base, Song Best Collection, and later 20th Anniversary Trade Please revivals.

narrative.human_title: Trade Please Campaign — the market becomes a card
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of the cleanest origin objects for the whole protocol idea. The campaign asked a person to choose a course, mail in cards, and receive back a new pair. Charizard, Blastoise, or Venusaur supplied the desire; Trade Please! supplied the joke and the ritual. The card market was not just around the object. It was printed into the object.

card_highlights.assembly_note: Trade Please! row 036 is the companion card for every course, and the one that turns the campaign mechanic into card text and card art.
card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Trade Please! is the thesis card. It is loud, strange, and almost self-aware: a card received through trading, about trading, illustrated through Imakuni?'s performance-world energy. For this marketplace project, it is practically a fossil of intent.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Trade Please! as Trade Please Campaign source slice row 036 and credits Imakuni? as illustrator/source metadata.

The local row credits Trade Please! to Imakuni? as source/provider metadata, and the earlier hand-authored unnumbered promo dossier also preserves Imakuni? as the local illustrator credit.
Trade Please! matters because it makes exchange itself collectible: a card about trade that arrived through a mail-in trade ritual.

Agents should preserve Trade Please! row 036, Torikaekko Please name, Imakuni? credit, campaign companion-card role, special-back identity, and distinction from later Trade Please revivals or generic Imakuni trainer cards.
